summary:
This bill is a joint resolution, which is a type of proposal for a law. It cancels a rule made by the Department of Education. The rule was about changing and forgiving federal student loans. Federal student loans are money the government lends to people to help pay for college.

The rule included a plan called "One-Time Federal Student Loan Debt Relief." This plan was shared on a website and in a document dated October 12, 2022.

If this bill becomes a law, it means Congress does not approve of the Department of Education's rule. The rule would "have no force or effect." This means the rule would be stopped and could not be used.

The bill notes that the Government Accountability Office (a group that checks how the government works) wrote a letter on March 17, 2023. The letter said the loan rule counts as a "rule" under a law called the Congressional Review Act. This act lets Congress vote to reject rules made by government departments.

The House of Representatives passed this bill on May 24, 2023. The Senate received it on May 30, 2023. If the Senate also passes it and the President signs it, the student loan relief rule would end.
